Definition: neuter of G5306 as adverb; more lately, i.e. eventually:--afterward, (at the) last (of all).
BiblicalUsage: Afterward is a small word that carries a whole change of mind. Hebrews 12:11 says no chastening seems joyful at the time, but afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness, John 13:36 has Jesus telling Peter he will follow afterward, and Mark 16:14 shows the Lord appearing afterward to the eleven as they sat at meat.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe afterward is where God does some of his best work, in the fruit that only shows up later.
RelatedEvents: The Last Supper; The Resurrection; Jesus Appears to the Disciples on Easter Evening
